title: Recommendation orchestration: workflow & wireframe notes
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes for a lightweight orchestration view inside Optimize that surfaces model-specific recommendations (batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles), lets engineers preview estimated unit-economics impact, and schedule/rollout changes with safety controls. This doc is a sketch + backlog seed, not final UX.

Background and constraints

- Goal: reduce per-token cost and tail latency for customer workloads while preserving output quality.
- Recommendations are produced by the inference advisor engine (offline jobs + live telemetry). We will show suggested actions grouped by impact/confidence.
- Surface must be readable by engineers and platform/product managers; cannot assume deep ML background.
- Must integrate with Dedicated and Private targets; some actions only available on Dedicated/private deployments.

Primary user personas

- Platform engineer (core persona): wants predictable unit economics, safe rollouts, and observability.
- ML engineer: wants to validate that quantization preserves quality on evaluation prompt sets.
- Product manager / SRE: wants to see risk & metrics, and to approve rollouts.

High level flows

1) Overview -> scan across models/routes -> act on high-impact suggestions.
2) Detail -> inspect recommendation, see metrics, preview simulation results, run eval, apply as draft or schedule.
3) Rollout -> canary A/B, gradual traffic shifting, automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency regressions.

Wireframe text descriptions (working)

A. Recommendations Overview (page)
- Top bar: time range selector, alignment to route/model, telemetry freshness indicator.
- Left column: model list with small sparkline for latency and cost, tag filters (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Middle column: grouped recommendations feed sorted by estimated monthly savings (descending). Each card shows: recommendation type (batching/caching/quantization), short summary, estimated savings (dollars/month and percent), confidence (high/medium/low), eyeball to open detail.
- Right column: live preview panel for selected recommendation. Shows current config vs suggested config in a diff-like view, quick pros/cons bullets, and 'Simulate' CTA.
- Empty state: if no recommendations, show checklist explaining why (insufficient telemetry, no compatible models, or disabled advisor).

B. Recommendation detail drawer/modal
- Header: recommendation title, impact and confidence chips.
- Left: expanded explanation (why this matters), links to related incidents or tickets.
- Center: numeric breakdown -> current throughput, expected throughput after change, 95th latency impact estimate, cost per 1M tokens before/after, and expected delta. Pull datas from estimator service.
- Right: action panel with three choices: Preview only (run simulation), Apply to route (draft), Schedule rollout. Each action shows gating requirements (e.g., test eval must pass for quantization).
- Inline mini-eval: small sample of prompts and model outputs under current vs suggested. Flag differences with colored diff markers. Note: for now show only 5 prompts to avoid large compute.

C. Apply / Rollout flow sketches
- Step 1: select targets (model, route, environment). Toggle between 'All matching routes' and manual pick.
- Step 2: choose strategy: immediate, canary percent (5/25/50), or schedule window. Show estimated savings per strategy and expected exposure.
- Step 3: risk controls: require manual approval, tie to alert thresholds (latency increase > 10% or quality drop measured by eval metric), automatic rollback setting.
- Confirmation: summary card with final estimated monthly savings and rollback window. Button: 'Schedule rollout' or 'Apply now'.

Microcopy and labels (working)

- Recommendation types: Batching optimization, Prefix caching (KV), Quantization profile.
- Confidence chips: High confidence, Needs eval, Exploratory.
- CTA: Simulate, Run sample eval, Apply draft, Schedule rollout, Create Jira.
- Tooltips: 'Estimated savings are based on telemetry and batching model heuristics; actual savings may vary.'

Backlog items (prioritized)

1) RI-3421 Recommendation aggregator API contract (critical) - produce summarized recommendations with savings estimates. (owner eng-applied-ml)
2) RI-3470 Recs UI overview page (MVP) - list + detail panels and simulation CTA. (owner product)
3) RI-3492 Mini-eval runner integration - add 5-prompt diff view for quantization recommendations. (owner eng-serving-runtime)
4) RI-3510 Rollout scheduling UI + approval workflow - include canary controls and rollback policies. (owner product-ops)
5) RI-3533 Dedicated/private gating flags - enable action buttons only for supported targets. (owner infra)
6) RI-3555 Estimator calibration jobs - surface confidence and margin-of-error. (owner applied-ml)

Acceptance criteria (MVP)

- Overview page lists at least model-level recommendations for any account with >= 24h telemetry.
- Detail drawer shows before/after cost and latency estimates and a run-simulation button.
- Users can create a rollout draft and see an approval required state.
- UI integrates with linear/GH to create linked tickets when a rollout is scheduled.

Metrics to track success

- Activation: number of accounts that view recommendations within 14 days of it being available.
- Adoption: percent of recommendations applied or scheduled within 30 days. Baseline target for MVP: 8% of recommendations.
- Accuracy: percent of simulations whose cost estimate is within 20% of realized costs after 30 days.
- Safety: percent of rollouts that require automated rollback. Target: <3% for MVP.

Open questions and discussion items

- What is the minimum telemetry window for confident batching suggestions? Can we offer low-confidence heuristics for new models? (ask applied-ml)
- For quantization, what is the gating evaluation metric (BLEU-like, embedding cosine, hallucination rate)? Need input from research.
- How do we compute savings for prefix caching when cache hit rates are dynamic and user-specific? Consider bounding with lower/upper estimates.
- Should 'apply draft' create an infrastructure PR for private deployments, or do we hand off to solutions engineering?

Immediate next steps (this week)

- Align with Diego and Rahul on API fields for estimator (RI-3421).
- Design quick mocks for overview cards and diff preview (Arielle). Link to GH draft PR for skeleton components.
- Create Linear tasks for mini-eval infra and rollout workflow (assign owners).
- Run 2 customer interviews focusing on platform engineers to validate risk controls and rollout mental model.

Notes to self / rough ideas

- Consider a single 'Apply as preset' action that packages batching+cache+quantization into a named preset that can be reviewed and shared. Presets could be audited in Console.
- If showing monetary savings, also show relative percent change and an estimate of time-to-payback for reserved capacity adjustments.
- Explore live-preview toggles that simulate only latency or only cost so user can focus on specific tradeoffs.

References and links

- Internal: confluence:Optimize-Recs-DesignSpace (linked above)
- Linear seed tasks: RI-3421, RI-3470, RI-3492
- Dev: github.com/redwood-inference/recs-ui (PR 88 is a basic skeleton)

End of working notes. This doc will evolve into a formal PRD once API shapes are finalized.
